$comment_devWorlds3: STAGING worlds in the world tree, maps2/worlds3/<name>/world.json
(pixel-maps3/world@1 — a ground NAME per cell, no baked tile art; tiles3
resolves what draws at draw time). None since 2026-09-09. A staging world
costs the image zero bytes: an admin joins it from the repo (client:
staging.ts via jsDelivr; server: WorldRoom's disk-first GitHub fallback).
Joining one also streams the tiles3 ART TREES (tiles/plates, tiles/patterns,
tiles/tops, tiles/fades, tiles/base_candidates, tiles/review + the index
JSONs) from the CDN through the same gameUrl chokepoint: they are served at
/assets/tiles/... and the image ships only the closure of its PUBLISHED
worlds3 worlds (userWorlds above), never the 400 MB domain.
$comment_monsters: Monsters reachable from a published world's spawns.json are found
automatically. This list is only for monsters the ENGINE names directly
with no spawn zone — leave empty unless something 404s.
$comment_scenery: The three pieces WorldScene loads by hardcoded path. The v2 factory's other
~2,640 pieces are staging content until the maps2 agent places them.
$comment_entityDomains: Domains where individual entities are selected by closure. Their ROOT-level
files and config/ trees ship wholesale regardless — those are descriptors the
404 a sprite, it silently empties a manifest: the first curated root built a
game with ZERO monsters for exactly this reason.
$comment_alwaysShip: Domains where per-entity closure buys little: items and lore are small and
wholly in-game, live/ is runtime tuning state, wiki/ is the wiki itself.
sounds/ and music/ are catalog-driven at runtime rather than referenced by
the worlds, so they ship whole minus the excludes below — tightening those
two to a real catalog closure is a follow-up, not a guess to make here.
$comment_exclude: Applied last, so these carve out of the wholesale alwaysShip includes.
The music masters are also excluded by .dockerignore — kept here so ONE file
is the source of truth for what ships.
